message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm p1 with $247 and the red monopoly. I'm checking opponent p3's properties to assess trade and build options.

p3 sold Virginia to p2. p2 now has St. Charles and Virginia for a pink monopoly. I can only build one house on the red properties with $247.

One house on Illinois would yield the highest rent. I'm weighing whether to mortgage Vermont and New York for extra cash.

Mortgaging Vermont and New York would give me $397. That covers two houses on the red set. I will mortgage those two properties to fund the houses.

I'll place one house on Illinois and one on Indiana. Illinois yields $100 rent, Indiana $90, while Kentucky stays at $36 without houses.

I'll mortgage New York and Vermont first to raise cash, then build houses on the red set. Illinois is the most landed-on property, so it's the best spot for a house.

New York is not blocking a near-complete orange set, since p3 lacks Tennessee. Vermont is a light blue property that could help complete a set if I acquire Oriental, but mortgaging it now sacrifices trade flexibility for immediate house funding.

I'll build one house now for $150, leaving $97. Then I'll mortgage New York and Vermont to raise the extra cash needed for a second house.

I'm now considering selling Vermont to p4 for cash instead of mortgaging it. p4 has $1005 and could fund the houses without losing the property permanently.

Mortgaging both properties still leaves me $53 short of the $450 needed for three houses. I'm now considering selling New York for cash to fund a third house, since its list price is $200 but its mortgage value is only $100.

No opponent is one card away from completing a monopoly that I hold. New York has no obvious buyer, so selling it for cash would not help me build houses.

Selling Vermont for $300 would raise cash to $547, enough for three houses. That would add only about $54 in rent per landing compared to two houses. The real spike is from two houses to three, which requires seven total houses and $1050 in construction costs. I cannot afford that many houses.

I'll mortgage Vermont and New York for $150. That still leaves $203 short of four houses, so selling New York would require overpaying. I'll keep the monopoly and mortgage the junk instead.

I'll mortgage New York first for $100, then Vermont for $50, and build the houses afterward. The order doesn't matter since opponents don't move during post-turn actions.

I'm now considering selling New York for $400 or more. That would give me $647, enough to build four houses at a 2/1/1 distribution. That yields $300 in rent from Illinois, $90 from Indiana, and $90 from Kentucky. That is far better than two houses on one property.

No opponent is likely to pay enough for New York to justify selling it. p3 lacks Tennessee, so the property does not complete an orange set. p4 warned against funding me, and p2 wants States rather than New York. A trade proposal would waste a turn, so I will mortgage the properties directly.

I'm now considering keeping New York unmortgaged as trade bait while mortgaging only Vermont. That would let me build one house immediately, but the second house on Indiana would still require the New York mortgage.
